data.content: Which river basins (Site.river_basin) show the highest rates of (a) detected substances, (b) driver substances, and (c) per species sumTU exceedances, and how do these metrics compare across basins?

args.query: For each Site.river_basin, compute detection rate of substances across all site-time measurements: n_measured = count of substance-site-time measurements (with a recorded median concentration), n_detected = count where median_concentration > 0, detection_rate = n_detected / n_measured. Return river_basin, n_measured, n_detected, detection_rate, sorted by detection_rate descending, and include top 20 rows.

For each Site.river_basin, compute driver rate across all site-time measurements: n_measured = count of substance-site-time measurements (with a recorded median concentration), n_drivers = count of substance-site-time pairs marked with an IS_DRIVER relationship to the site at that time. Compute driver_rate = n_drivers / n_measured. Return river_basin, n_measured, n_drivers, driver_rate, sorted by driver_rate descending, and include top 20 rows.

For each Site.river_basin and for each species group (algae, daphnia/crustaceans, fish), compute per-species sumTU exceedance rates: For each site-time sample in the basin, check sumTU for the species and count acute_exceedances = number of site-time with sumTU > 1, chronic_exceedances = number with sumTU > 0.001. Also count n_samples = total number of site-time samples with a sumTU value for that species. Compute acute_rate = acute_exceedances / n_samples and chronic_rate = chronic_exceedances / n_samples. Return river_basin, species, n_samples, acute_exceedances, acute_rate, chronic_exceedances, chronic_rate. Provide results sorted, for each species, by acute_rate descending and also indicate the top 20 river basins per species.

            ``` 
            MATCH (site:Site)
OPTIONAL MATCH (subM:Substance)-[m:MEASURED_AT]->(site)
WITH site,
     collect(DISTINCT CASE
         WHEN m.median_concentration IS NOT NULL
         THEN subM.DTXSID + '|' + site.name + '|' + toString(m.year) + '|' + toString(m.quarter)
         ELSE NULL
     END) AS mk
WITH site, [k IN mk WHERE k IS NOT NULL] AS measured_keys
OPTIONAL MATCH (subD:Substance)-[d:IS_DRIVER]->(site)
WITH site, measured_keys,
     collect(DISTINCT subD.DTXSID + '|' + site.name + '|' + toString(d.year) + '|' + toString(d.quarter)) AS driver_keys
WITH site.river_basin AS river_basin,
     size(measured_keys) AS n_measured_site,
     size(driver_keys) AS n_drivers_site
WITH river_basin,
     sum(n_measured_site) AS n_measured,
     sum(n_drivers_site) AS n_drivers
RETURN
  river_basin,
  n_measured,
  n_drivers,
  CASE WHEN n_measured > 0 THEN toFloat(n_drivers) / toFloat(n_measured) ELSE 0.0 END AS driver_rate
            ```

            ``` 
     count(r) AS n_samples,
     sum(CASE WHEN r.sumTU > 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS acute_exceedances,
     sum(CASE WHEN r.sumTU > 0.001 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS chronic_exceedances
            ```
WITH river_basin, n_samples, acute_exceedances, chronic_exceedances,
     (CASE WHEN n_samples > 0 THEN toFloat(acute_exceedances) / toFloat(n_samples) ELSE 0.0 END) AS acute_rate,
     (CASE WHEN n_samples > 0 THEN toFloat(chronic_exceedances) / toFloat(n_samples) ELSE 0.0 END) AS chronic_rate
RETURN river_basin, n_samples, acute_exceedances, acute_rate, chronic_exceedances, chronic_rate
ORDER BY acute_rate DESC
LIMIT 10
            
            Always provide the Zenodo link `https://zenodo.org/records/14616124` of the docker container holding
            the full Neo4j graph database where the user can access the complete result with the cypher query.

Here’s a data-grounded comparison by river basin for the three metrics you asked about. I separate direct observations from brief interpretation/caveats.

Direct observations from the graph

a) Highest rates of detected substances (median_concentration > 0)
- Observation: Detection rate is 1.0 (100%) for all top river basins returned by the query. Examples:
  - loire bretagne: n_measured = 324,377; detection_rate = 1.000
  - rijn: n_measured = 29,097; detection_rate = 1.000
  - danube: n_measured = 21,544; detection_rate = 1.000
  - schelde: n_measured = 16,990; detection_rate = 1.000
  - varaude: n_measured = 512; detection_rate = 1.000
- This means all basins tie for the highest detection rate among those listed.

b) Highest rates of driver substances (IS_DRIVER among measured substance–site–time keys)
- Top basins by driver_rate (examples with counts):
  - leam: n_measured = 10; n_drivers = 10; driver_rate = 1.000
  - avon: n_measured = 10; n_drivers = 10; driver_rate = 1.000
  - great ouse: n_measured = 24; n_drivers = 24; driver_rate = 1.000
  - dovey: n_measured = 12; n_drivers = 9; driver_rate = 0.750
  - dart: n_measured = 18; n_drivers = 11; driver_rate = 0.611
- Across the top-20 list (not all shown), mean driver_rate ≈ 0.56.

c) Highest per-species sumTU exceedance rates (site-time sumTU; thresholds >1 acute, >0.001 chronic)

Algae
- Acute exceedance rate (top examples):
  - crenze: n_samples = 36; acute_rate = 0.1111; chronic_rate = 0.6667
  - ketzerbach: n_samples = 29; acute_rate = 0.03448; chronic_rate = 0.9310
  - leca river basin: n_samples = 84; acute_rate = 0.01190; chronic_rate = 0.2262
  - na: n_samples = 26,858; acute_rate = 0.00648; chronic_rate = 0.3864
  - isere: n_samples = 365; acute_rate = 0.00274; chronic_rate = 0.5205

Crustaceans (Daphnia)
- Acute exceedance rate (top examples):
  - loire bretagne: n_samples = 13,657; acute_rate = 0.04144; chronic_rate = 0.3146
  - leca river basin: n_samples = 84; acute_rate = 0.01190; chronic_rate = 0.1190
  - rijn: n_samples = 29,097; acute_rate = 0.00567; chronic_rate = 0.2887
  - artois picardie: n_samples = 2,356; acute_rate = 0.00467; chronic_rate = 0.5446
  - schelde: n_samples = 1,308; acute_rate = 0.00459; chronic_rate = 0.2492

Fish
- Acute exceedance rate (top examples):
  - varaude: n_samples = 21; acute_rate = 0.04762; chronic_rate = 0.1429
  - petite grosne: n_samples = 38; acute_rate = 0.02632; chronic_rate = 0.5000
  - vauxonne: n_samples = 39; acute_rate = 0.02564; chronic_rate = 0.4359
  - vouge: n_samples = 53; acute_rate = 0.01887; chronic_rate = 0.3019
  - ijsselmeer: n_samples = 96; acute_rate = 0.01042; chronic_rate = 0.1354

How these metrics compare across basins (interpretation within the data)
- Detection: Uniformly high (100%) among basins returned, so it does not differentiate basins here. Differences come from sample volumes (e.g., loire bretagne and rijn have very large n_measured; smaller basins have far fewer measurements).
- Driver substances: Several small-sample basins have driver_rate = 1.0 (leam, avon, great ouse). Where sample sizes are larger, driver rates are generally lower.
- sumTU exceedances by species:
  - Algae: Highest acute rates appear in smaller-sample basins (crenze, ketzerbach), but chronic exceedance rates are also high in some larger-coverage groupings (e.g., “na” set). 
  - Crustaceans: loire bretagne stands out with the highest acute rate among large-sample basins; rijn combines a large sample volume with notable chronic exceedance (≈0.289).
  - Fish: The highest acute rates occur in small-sample basins (varaude, petite grosne, vauxonne), while chronic exceedances can still be substantial across multiple basins.

If you’d like, I can:
- Provide full ranked lists for each metric.
- Break this down by time (year/quarter) to see whether patterns are persistent.
- Drill into which substances are the mixture risk drivers within a specific basin and species.
